name: Art Mod
classification_notes: A geometric sans in the Art Deco vein, sitting alongside Anisette in Porchez's run of typefaces inspired by 1920s and 30s French lettering.
summary: A geometric Art Deco sans that trades Anisette's curl for straighter, more architectural strokes.
description: Art Mod runs from a hairline to a solid black across nine weights, built on the same 1920s and 30s reference points that shape much of Porchez's display work. It reads as a plainer companion to Anisette, less playful, more structural, suited to headlines and branding that want period character without novelty.
foundry_blurb: Typofonderie present Art Mod as a contemporary reading of Art Deco geometry, offered across nine weights for graphic designers and art directors.

name: Ardent
classification_notes: An Elzevir-family old-style serif engineered for screen reading, with triangular serifs Porchez traces back to inscriptions in the Paris catacombs.
summary: A screen-first Elzevir serif with triangular serifs borrowed from Parisian catacomb lettering.
description: Ardent takes the old-style Elzevir tradition and rebuilds it for legibility at small sizes on screen. Its triangular serifs and rounded drops nod to engraved inscriptions Porchez studied in the Paris catacombs, and nine weights with italics give it range across text and display.
foundry_blurb: Typofonderie describe Ardent as a synthesis of several typefaces that marked the history of typography, engineered for excellent on-screen readability.

name: Former
classification_notes: A nine-weight contemporary sans by Raphaël Ronot, published through Typofonderie rather than designed in-house by Porchez.
summary: A nine-weight contemporary sans built for general professional use, from Typofonderie designer Raphaël Ronot.
description: Former covers the full range from Thin to Black with matching italics, aimed at graphic designers and art directors who need a dependable working sans. It has no particular quirk to sell, just even coverage across the weight range.
foundry_blurb: Typofonderie position Former as a typeface for professionals, graphic designers and art directors, as well as typography enthusiasts, with a design suited to today's taste.

name: Akhen
classification_notes: Sold as three narrow widths, Compressed, Condensed and Narrow, rather than a standard-width cut. Reworks the French égyptienne tradition, what English calls slab serif, after 19th-century metal and wood types.
summary: A trio of narrow égyptienne widths remixing 19th-century French slab serif types for tight, asymmetrical layouts.
description: Akhen only ships in narrow builds, Compressed, Condensed and Narrow, each running the full weight range. It takes its cue from 19th-century French metal and wood égyptiennes, the French term for slab serifs, and its tight fit suits headline work where space is short.
foundry_blurb: Typofonderie call Akhen an Egypto-typographic remix, paying homage to French égyptienne types with tight spacing built for asymmetrical layouts.

name: Aukio
classification_notes: A contemporary serif by Léo Guibert, one of the newer names publishing through Typofonderie.
summary: A contemporary text serif from newer Typofonderie name Léo Guibert.
description: Aukio is one of the newest additions to the Typofonderie catalogue, a serif built for current taste rather than any particular revival brief. Details beyond the regular weight are thin on the ground, reflecting how recently it launched.
foundry_blurb: Typofonderie introduce Aukio as a new typeface designed to meet a contemporary aesthetic.

name: Airco
subcategory: ultra-slanted italic and script hybrid, with sans companion
classification_notes: Sold as a single Bold Italic weight in two cuts, Airco and Airco Sans, sitting between italic and script with a 27-degree slant drawn from Renaissance italic models.
summary: An ultra-slanted italic-script hybrid, tilted 27 degrees, with a companion sans-serif cut.
description: Airco pushes a single Bold Italic weight hard: rounded terminals, a steep 27-degree slant, and letterforms rooted in Renaissance italics but pulled toward script. Airco Sans strips the same movement back to a sans-serif companion.
foundry_blurb: Typofonderie describe Airco as sitting between italic and script styles, with shapes that evoke fast, assertive movement.

name: Alembert
subcategory: calligraphic swash script, Bâtardes and Coulées revival
classification_notes: Draws on 17th and 18th-century Bâtardes and Coulées scripts, the Maîtres écrivains tradition, bridging italic and English script conventions.
summary: A calligraphic script built on 17th and 18th-century French Bâtardes and Coulées models.
description: Alembert sits between italic and English script, offering formal capitals alongside larger swash capitals for use as initials. Extensive OpenType alternates let it recreate the flourishes of the Maîtres écrivains, France's historic master penmen.
foundry_blurb: Typofonderie present Alembert as an exploration of the Maîtres écrivains, with formal and swash capitals designed to be paired freely with the lowercase.

name: Altesse
classification_notes: A formal copperplate script offered in five optical sizes rather than weights, matching Porchez's habit of scaling display faces by size rather than boldness.
summary: A formal copperplate script scaled across five optical sizes rather than weights.
description: Altesse draws on copperplate engraving traditions for formal, ceremonial settings: invitations, certificates, packaging with a heritage air. Instead of a weight range it offers five optical sizes, from a fine 16pt cut up to a bolder 96pt display size.
foundry_blurb: Typofonderie offer Altesse as a formal script family in five optical sizes, refined for professional graphic design and typography use.

name: Alyssa
classification_notes: A single-weight display face by Mark De Winne mixing incised, engraved detail with calligraphic gesture, meant to be set large.
summary: A single-weight display face pairing incised detail with calligraphic gesture, built to be set big.
description: Alyssa keeps to one weight and puts its energy into the letter shapes: bold, exaggerated details offset by looser calligraphic strokes. It is designed for large sizes, logotypes and magazine spreads, where the word shapes it creates can do the work.
foundry_blurb: Typofonderie describe Alyssa as a dynamic single-weight display typeface that brings flair and sophistication to logotypes, magazine spreads and branding.

name: Ambroise
classification_notes: Every cut in the family is named after a member of the Didot printing dynasty. Ambroise Firmin is the condensed width and Ambroise François the extra-condensed width of this same design, not separate typefaces.
summary: A Didot-style display serif named for the Didot printing dynasty, with condensed and extra-condensed widths built in.
description: Ambroise takes high-contrast Didot forms and gives them a full width range: standard, the condensed Firmin, and the extra-condensed François. Seven weights with italics cover the family, all tracing their names to members of the historic Didot printing house.
foundry_blurb: Typofonderie describe Ambroise Pro's rebirth as fifteen years in the making, tightly connected to the Didot dynasty of French type founders and printers.

name: Angie Sans
classification_notes: The sans-serif half of the Angie superfamily, a separate design from the serif FF Angie rather than a rebrand of it.
summary: The sans-serif companion in the Angie superfamily, a separate design from its serif sibling FF Angie.
description: Angie Sans covers Regular, Demi and Bold with italics, built to pair alongside FF Angie rather than replace it. It is the plainer half of the two, useful where the serif's Open swash detailing would be too much.
foundry_blurb: Typofonderie list Angie Sans as an associated family to FF Angie, extending the Angie project into sans-serif territory.

name: FF Angie
subcategory: display serif with open and swash cut
classification_notes: Originally issued through FontFont, hence the FF prefix retained in the name. A distinct serif design from its sans companion Angie Sans, not an older release of the same face.
summary: A display serif with an open, illuminated Black Open cut, the serif half of the Angie superfamily.
description: FF Angie runs from Regular to Black with italics throughout, plus a Black Open style that hollows the counters for a lit-up display effect. It keeps the FF prefix from its original FontFont-era release, and pairs with the separate sans design Angie Sans.
foundry_blurb: Typofonderie list Angie Sans as an associated family alongside FF Angie, the serif original released under the FontFont label.

name: Anisette
classification_notes: An Art Deco geometric sans in nine weights, with Anisette Petite as its optical-size companion for smaller text settings.
summary: A nine-weight Art Deco geometric sans, with Petite as its optical size for smaller text.
description: Anisette pulls its geometry from 1920s and 30s Art Deco lettering, running Thin to Black with matching italics. Anisette Petite adjusts the same design for smaller sizes, tightening spacing and opening counters so it holds up at text scale.
foundry_blurb: Typofonderie present Anisette as an Art Deco typeface, a geometric sanserif in nine weights.

name: Apolline
classification_notes: One of Porchez's earliest releases, an old-style text serif in the Garamond tradition dating to Typofonderie's founding year.
summary: An old-style text serif in the Garamond tradition, one of Typofonderie's founding-year typefaces.
description: Apolline has been in the Typofonderie catalogue since the foundry's first year, a humanist old-style serif built for long-form text. Five weights with italics keep it flexible for books and editorial work without straying from its historical roots.
foundry_blurb: Typofonderie list Apolline among their original 1994 catalogue, a text serif built for setting substantial bodies of copy.

name: Arbale
classification_notes: A geometric sans offered in three tones, Modern, Universal and Vernacular, via OpenType, extended to Cyrillic and Greek in the 2023 Pro release.
summary: A geometric sans that switches between Modern, Universal and Vernacular tones, now covering Latin, Cyrillic and Greek.
description: Arbale mixes modernist geometric construction with 20th-century vernacular lettering, bundling three stylistic tones into one OpenType family so the same text can read as clean and modern or hand-lettered and vernacular. The 2023 Pro update added full Cyrillic and Greek.
foundry_blurb: Typofonderie describe Arbale as modern, universal and vernacular: a hybrid geometric sans built for style and identity while staying comfortable as a text face.

name: Ardoise
classification_notes: An homage to Roger Excoffon's Antique Olive, evolved from Porchez's earlier 1999 design Charente and revamped for the redesign of Pèlerin magazine. Sold in standard, Narrow, Tight and Compact widths.
summary: A humanist sans paying homage to Roger Excoffon's Antique Olive, built for newspaper work in four widths.
description: Ardoise grew out of Charente, a 1999 Porchez design later reworked in 2010 for the French magazine Pèlerin. It shares Antique Olive's warmth and open counters, and comes in standard, Narrow, Tight and Compact widths to handle everything from body text to tight headline settings.
foundry_blurb: Typofonderie present Ardoise as simple, tense shapes designed to renew and revitalise, an organic homage to Roger Excoffon's work.

name: Arsen
classification_notes: A French Elzevir built with heavy reference to the Turlot foundry's Elzevir No.3 of 1895, offered across four optical sizes, Affiche, Display, Normal and Text.
summary: A French Elzevir built from the Turlot foundry's 1895 Elzevir No.3, scaled across four optical sizes.
description: Arsen is not a strict revival, it takes heavy influence from Turlot's Elzevir No.3 without reproducing any one historical style outright. Four optical sizes, Affiche for posters down to Text for body copy, each carry seven styles in roman and italic.
foundry_blurb: Typofonderie call Arsen a new French Elzevir, the result of research by Joachim Vu into the Parisian Turlot foundry's cuts of around 1895.

name: Arteria Compress
subcategory: compressed vernacular display, Italian signage and woodtype
classification_notes: Only issued as a compressed cut, no standard-width Arteria exists. The design merges Italian shopfront lettering with woodtype poster conventions.
summary: A compressed display face fusing Italian shopfront lettering with woodtype poster conventions.
description: Arteria Compress takes two related vernacular traditions, hand-spaced capitals on Italian shopfronts and the geometric simplicity of woodtype posters, and runs them through nine weights of tightly fitted capitals. No standard width was ever released; compressed is the only cut.
foundry_blurb: Typofonderie describe Arteria as evoking the way capitals are used on Italian shop fronts and public buildings, alongside the wood type style seen on posters and billboards.

name: Astronef
classification_notes: An eight-width geometric sans superfamily, from Super down to Compressed, built as one coordinated system rather than separate typefaces.
summary: A geometric modernist sans built as one coordinated system across eight widths, from Super to Compressed.
description: Astronef, French for spaceship, treats width as the whole design brief: eight coordinated cuts running from an ultra-wide Super down to a tight Compressed, all sharing the same modernist geometric bones. It reads as a toolkit rather than a single typeface, useful anywhere a project needs one family to cover generous and cramped spaces alike.
foundry_blurb: Typofonderie describe Astronef as a modernist sans serif spanning multiple widths, an ode to futuristic design.

name: Austerlitz
classification_notes: A Parisian Didot system in four optical sizes, Affiche, Gros, Labeur and Petit, running from poster-scale contrast down to a humble, highly legible small size.
summary: A charming Parisian Didot scaled across four optical sizes, from poster contrast down to a humble text size.
description: Austerlitz takes the Didot high-contrast tradition and splits it into four purpose-built sizes: Affiche for posters, Gros and Labeur for general and ordinary Didot use, and Petit for small, legible settings. Each size is tuned rather than simply scaled from the others.
foundry_blurb: Typofonderie describe Austerlitz across its four sizes: a high-contrast Parisian Didot for posters, a charming Gros, the ordinary Labeur by excellence, and a humble, highly legible Petit.

name: AW Conqueror Carved
subcategory: carved and engraved display, AW Conqueror collection
classification_notes: Part of the AW Conqueror collection, a toolbox of related display treatments. Carved applies an engraved, chiselled texture rather than sharing letterforms with the collection's other cuts.
summary: A carved, engraved-look display face from the AW Conqueror collection.
description: AW Conqueror Carved layers a chiselled, engraved texture over its letterforms, with a Regular plus four numbered depth variants standing in for weights. It belongs to the wider AW Conqueror toolbox of display treatments rather than sharing a skeleton with its siblings.
foundry_blurb: Typofonderie position AW Conqueror Carved within the AW Conqueror collection, a typeface toolbox for everyone.

name: AW Conqueror Didot
subcategory: Didot display serif, AW Conqueror collection
classification_notes: The core Didot-style cut in the AW Conqueror collection, distinct from the Large and Small optical variants sold alongside it.
summary: A modern Didot interpretation and the core cut of the AW Conqueror collection.
description: AW Conqueror Didot runs eight weights from Light to Black, a contemporary take on classical Didot proportions built for professional display and editorial work. It sits alongside Didot Large and Didot Small as one of three optical variants in the collection.
foundry_blurb: Typofonderie present AW Conqueror as a typeface toolbox for everyone, with Didot as its classical modern-serif cut.

name: AW Conqueror Didot Large
subcategory: Didot display serif, large optical size
classification_notes: The large-size optical variant of AW Conqueror Didot, tuned for bigger display settings rather than body text.
summary: The large-format optical cut of AW Conqueror Didot, tuned for bigger display sizes.
description: AW Conqueror Didot Large adjusts the collection's core Didot design for bigger settings, refining stroke contrast so it holds together at poster and headline scale. Eight weights match the standard cut.
foundry_blurb: Typofonderie offer AW Conqueror Didot Large as the display-scale optical size within the AW Conqueror collection.

name: AW Conqueror Didot Small
subcategory: Didot text serif, small optical size
classification_notes: The small-size optical variant of AW Conqueror Didot, adjusted for text rather than display use.
summary: The text-optimised small optical cut of AW Conqueror Didot.
description: AW Conqueror Didot Small carries the collection's Didot proportions down to text sizes, opening the counters and easing the contrast so it stays legible in body copy. Eight weights match the rest of the Didot set.
foundry_blurb: Typofonderie offer AW Conqueror Didot Small as the text-scale optical size within the AW Conqueror collection.

name: AW Conqueror Inline
classification_notes: An inline decorative treatment within the AW Conqueror collection.
summary: An inline decorative display face from the AW Conqueror collection.
description: AW Conqueror Inline cuts a fine line through each letterform for a decorative, layered look at large sizes. It is one of the toolbox of display treatments sharing the AW Conqueror name.
foundry_blurb: Typofonderie place AW Conqueror Inline within the AW Conqueror collection, a typeface toolbox for everyone.

name: AW Conqueror Sans
classification_notes: The geometric sans-serif cut in the AW Conqueror collection, launched in 2022.
summary: A geometric sans with refined proportions, the sans-serif cut of the AW Conqueror collection.
description: AW Conqueror Sans brings a clean geometric structure to the collection, with eight weights and italics giving it enough range for both text and display work.
foundry_blurb: Typofonderie present AW Conqueror Sans as the geometric sans-serif member of the AW Conqueror toolbox.

name: AW Conqueror Slab
classification_notes: The slab serif cut in the AW Conqueror collection.
summary: A slab serif cut of the AW Conqueror collection, built for sturdy headline work.
description: AW Conqueror Slab applies heavy, even slab serifs to the collection's shared proportions, giving it the weight and presence to anchor a headline or logotype.
foundry_blurb: Typofonderie present AW Conqueror Slab as the slab-serif member of the AW Conqueror toolbox.

name: AW Conqueror Stincilla
classification_notes: A stencil treatment within the AW Conqueror collection, launched in 2022.
summary: A chic stencil display face and part of the AW Conqueror collection.
description: AW Conqueror Stincilla breaks its letterforms into stencil segments across eight weights, described by the foundry as chic and full of surprises. It is built for display use rather than running text.
foundry_blurb: Typofonderie describe AW Conqueror Stincilla as chic and full of surprises, a stencil member of the AW Conqueror toolbox.

name: Basco
classification_notes: Bruno Mello's first Typofonderie release, a Renaissance-influenced serif with asymmetrical, calligraphic serif detailing across nine weights.
summary: A Renaissance-influenced serif with calligraphic, subtly asymmetrical serifs, Bruno Mello's first release for the foundry.
description: Basco reads as a contemporary take on Renaissance handwriting, its letterforms shaped by the period's calligraphy rather than any single revival source. Nine weights with italics give it a full working range, with a Mediterranean, tropical warmth in the details.
foundry_blurb: Typofonderie describe Basco as a mix of Renaissance and tropical atmosphere, the first typeface from São Paulo-based designer Bruno Mello.

name: Capek
classification_notes: A contemporary serif by Aurélien Vret, one of Typofonderie's guest designers.
summary: A contemporary serif from Typofonderie guest designer Aurélien Vret.
description: Capek is a comparatively quiet release in the catalogue, built to current taste without an obvious revival source. It sits alongside a run of similarly new designs, Aukio, Alyssa and Zingiber among them.
foundry_blurb: Typofonderie publish Capek as part of its ongoing series of new typefaces designed to match today's taste.

name: Costa
classification_notes: A sans-serif with a twist: capitals stay close to pure sans models while several lowercase letters carry a small ending serif, a soft brush effect rather than a true serif. Began as a bespoke 1999 design for Costa Crociere before its 2004 general release.
summary: A Mediterranean-style sans with a brush-like ending serif on select lowercase letters, born as a bespoke face for an Italian cruise line.
description: Costa mixes the purity of Greek capitals with the softness of Renaissance script, giving its capitals a clean sans-serif structure while several lowercase letters, the a, n and d among them, pick up a small brush-stroke serif. It started in 1999 as a bespoke typeface for Costa Crociere before Typofonderie released it generally in 2004.
foundry_blurb: Typofonderie describe Costa as a Mediterranean-style sanserif, first designed for the Italian cruise line Costa Crociere.

name: Deréon
subcategory: swash display serif for fashion branding
classification_notes: Originally a bespoke typeface for Beyoncé's fashion label House of Deréon, made generally available through Typofonderie in 2025. Sober in its basic form but built to unfold into swash letters.
summary: A swash-capable display serif originally commissioned for Beyoncé's fashion label House of Deréon.
description: Deréon keeps its everyday form sober, a working serif for basic settings, but its swash letters unfold into loops and volutes for logotypes and headline use. It was designed as a bespoke face for the House of Deréon fashion label before Typofonderie made it generally available.
foundry_blurb: Typofonderie describe Deréon as a hybrid typeface, sober in its basic version but unfolding curves and volutes through its swash letters; it won a Creative Review Type Award.

name: Geneo
subcategory: slab serif on an oblique axis
classification_notes: A slab serif built on an oblique construction axis, sitting between Garamond-style transitional forms and 19th-century Egyptian slab serifs such as Rockwell or Boton.
summary: An oblique-axis slab serif blending Renaissance elegance with 19th-century Egyptian slab robustness.
description: Geneo sits halfway between classic Garamond and Transitional forms and the Egyptian slab serifs popular in the 19th century, its subtle contrast built on an oblique construction axis rather than a vertical one. Nine weights with italics earned Stéphane Elbaz a Type Directors Club Certificate of Excellence.
foundry_blurb: Typofonderie describe Geneo as a synthesis of historic and present-day typography, published as a new design by Stéphane Elbaz.

name: Le Monde Courrier
classification_notes: Part of the Le Monde newspaper superfamily, a proportional serif with typewriter-inspired character used for the paper's special sections. A genuinely distinct design from Le Monde Journal, Livre and Sans, not a style variant of any of them.
summary: A typewriter-flavoured proportional serif, one of five distinct designs in the Le Monde newspaper superfamily.
description: Le Monde Courrier borrows the character of typewriter faces without being monospaced, giving the newspaper a set of forms for quotes and special material distinct from its main text serif. It was a Bukva:raz prizewinner in 2001, alongside Le Monde Journal.
foundry_blurb: Typofonderie built Le Monde Courrier as part of the bespoke family designed for the French newspaper Le Monde, awarded at Bukva:raz 2001.

name: Le Monde Journal
classification_notes: The workhorse text serif of the Le Monde superfamily, designed for small newsprint sizes. A distinct design from Livre, Sans and Courrier, sharing only the family name.
summary: The economical text serif built for Le Monde's small newsprint sizes, and the best-known face in the Le Monde superfamily.
description: Le Monde Journal was built to survive newsprint's worst conditions: bigger counters, sturdy serifs, and enough character to stay recognisable at very small sizes. It won a Bukva:raz prize in 2001 and remains Porchez's best-known editorial serif.
foundry_blurb: Typofonderie describe Le Monde Journal as an economical, workhorse typeface adapted to any extreme condition of newspaper use.

name: Le Monde Livre
classification_notes: A higher-contrast serif in the Le Monde superfamily built for headlines and book-style setting rather than small newsprint text, distinct from Le Monde Journal though sharing the family's editorial brief.
summary: A higher-contrast serif in the Le Monde superfamily, built for headlines and book-style setting.
description: Le Monde Livre carries more contrast than its Journal sibling, suited to headlines and longer-form book work rather than tight newsprint columns. Le Monde Livre Classic later extended it with more traditional proportions.
foundry_blurb: Typofonderie built Le Monde Livre as part of the bespoke family designed for the French newspaper Le Monde.

name: Le Monde Livre Classic
classification_notes: A 1999 extension of Le Monde Livre with more classical proportions, sold as its own product within the Le Monde superfamily rather than a style variant.
summary: A 1999 extension of Le Monde Livre with more classical proportions, for editorial and book settings.
description: Le Monde Livre Classic dials back some of Livre's more modern details in favour of proportions closer to traditional book serifs, giving the Le Monde family a warmer option for long-form editorial work.
foundry_blurb: Typofonderie extended the Le Monde family with Livre Classic, refining its proportions for professional editorial and typography use.

name: Le Monde Sans
classification_notes: The sans-serif member of the Le Monde superfamily, designed as a companion to the serif faces for the newspaper's redesign.
summary: The humanist sans companion to Le Monde's serif faces, built for captions and secondary newspaper text.
description: Le Monde Sans gives the newspaper's serif family a sans-serif partner, humanist in structure rather than geometric, with nine weights and italics for use across captions, tables and secondary text.
foundry_blurb: Typofonderie built Le Monde Sans as the sans-serif member of the bespoke family designed for the French newspaper Le Monde.

name: Mencken
classification_notes: An American Scotch Roman remixed in the French tradition, sold in standard and Narrow widths plus Head and Text optical sizes, with Head Narrow and Head Compress as further width and optical combinations.
summary: An American Scotch Roman remixed à la française, spanning narrow widths and Head and Text optical sizes.
description: Mencken takes the 19th-century Scotch Roman, the transitional serif style used across American and Scottish newspapers, and reworks it with French sensibility. Head and Text optical sizes cover display and body use, while Narrow and Head Compress tighten it for constrained layouts.
foundry_blurb: Typofonderie describe Mencken as an American Scotch typeface remixed à la française.

name: Mislab
classification_notes: A contemporary grotesque by Xavier Dupré, sold with Narrow and Compact companion widths.
summary: A contemporary grotesque by Xavier Dupré, with Narrow and Compact widths for tighter settings.
description: Mislab has been in the Typofonderie catalogue since 2013 and picked up a Typography Annual Award of Excellence the following year. Its Narrow and Compact companions extend the same grotesque design into tighter spaces without redrawing it from scratch.
foundry_blurb: Typofonderie published Mislab, a new design by Xavier Dupré, exclusively through the foundry from spring 2013.

name: Parisine
classification_notes: A humanist sans built on Helvetica Bold's proportions but condensed to 90 percent and opened up for legibility, designed for RATP Paris Metro signage in 1996 and later extended into Narrow, Compress, Office and Plus sub-releases for wider communication use.
summary: The humanist sans designed for Paris Metro signage, now one of the city's visual symbols alongside Johnston in London and Helvetica in New York.
description: Parisine started in 1996 as a custom Bold and Bold Italic for RATP, based on Helvetica Bold's proportions but condensed to 90 percent with softer, rounder counters to keep it legible at small sizes. It grew into a full family by 1999, with Narrow, Compress, Office and Plus versions extending it for maps and general communication.
foundry_blurb: Typofonderie note that Parisine has become, over the years, one of the symbols of Paris, comparable to Johnston for the London Underground or Helvetica for the New York Subway.

name: Prosaic
classification_notes: Described by the foundry as a postmodern vernacular sans, nine weights by Aurélien Vret.
summary: A postmodern vernacular sans in nine weights, from Typofonderie designer Aurélien Vret.
description: Prosaic leans into an unpolished, vernacular character rather than grotesque neutrality, while still holding together as a working text face across its full Thin-to-Black range with italics.
foundry_blurb: Typofonderie describe Prosaic as a Postmodern vernacular sanserif, designed to match a contemporary aesthetic.

name: PS Fournier
classification_notes: Named after 18th-century French type founder Pierre Simon Fournier as a reference point rather than a strict historical revival, sold with Grand and Petit optical-size companions.
summary: An old-style serif inspired by 18th-century French founder Pierre Simon Fournier, in Grand and Petit optical sizes.
description: PS Fournier takes its name and general spirit from Pierre Simon Fournier rather than reviving one specific historical cut, giving Stéphane Elbaz room to design a working contemporary serif. Grand and Petit optical sizes extend it from display down to smaller text.
foundry_blurb: Typofonderie present PS Fournier as a contemporary design by Stéphane Elbaz built for professional graphic design and typography.

name: Retiro
subcategory: Didot, Hispanic variant, single weight across optical sizes
classification_notes: A single-weight Didot based on Ambroise, adapted with a Hispanic sensibility for the Spanish magazine Madriz, spanning five optical sizes rather than a weight range.
summary: A full-of-life Hispanic Didot, built for Madrid magazine Madriz and named after the city's Retiro park.
description: Retiro began as a bespoke Didot for Madriz magazine in the mid-2000s, based on Ambroise but reworked with a Hispanic character. Rather than a weight range it kept a single weight and instead built five optical sizes, 16pt up to 96pt, to hold contrast steady across a page.
foundry_blurb: Typofonderie describe Retiro as a full-of-life Hispanic Didot in five optical sizes, named after a park in Madrid.

name: Sabon Next
designer: Jan Tschichold (original design); revived and extended by Jean François Porchez
subcategory: old-style and transitional serif, Garalde revival
classification_notes: Porchez's licensed revival and extension of Jan Tschichold's 1960s Sabon, adding a Display cut and additional weights to the original two-weight design.
summary: Porchez's revival and extension of Jan Tschichold's Sabon, adding weights and a Display cut to the 1960s original.
description: Sabon Next keeps Tschichold's Garalde old-style structure intact while filling out what the original never had, a proper weight range and a Display size built for larger settings. It remains one of the more conservative entries in the catalogue, for readers who want Sabon rather than a reinterpretation of it.
foundry_blurb: Typofonderie present Sabon Next as a revival and extension of Jan Tschichold's classic Sabon, licensed for contemporary use.

name: Ysans
classification_notes: A geometric sans influenced by A.M. Cassandre lettering, originally designed for Yves Saint Laurent Beauty under the name Singulier. Ysans Mondrian is a multi-layer OpenType SVG colour version of the same letterforms, not a separate design.
summary: A geometric fashion sans influenced by A.M. Cassandre, still used by Yves Saint Laurent Beauty under its original name Singulier.
description: Ysans began in 2011 as a bespoke typeface for Yves Saint Laurent Beauty, with several letters, the R, narrow U, and pointed f and t, drawn as a direct homage to the YSL logo. Ysans Mondrian is the same design rebuilt as a multi-layer colour font, named after Saint Laurent's Mondrian dress, and offered free for display headlines.
foundry_blurb: Typofonderie describe Ysans as a sans influenced by Cassandre lettering and the geometric sans genre, still in use by Yves Saint Laurent Beauty under its original name.

name: Zingiber
classification_notes: An elegant, relaxed script by Xavier Dupré, released as part of Typofonderie's 30th anniversary collection.
summary: An elegant, relaxed script with a handcrafted feel, released for Typofonderie's 30th anniversary.
description: Zingiber shows off Xavier Dupré's calligraphy training, a script that keeps a loose, handwritten quality rather than the tight regularity of a formal copperplate. It joined the catalogue as part of Typofonderie's 30th anniversary collection.
foundry_blurb: Typofonderie present Zingiber as an elegant yet relaxed script showcasing a handcrafted design touch.

name: Aiglon
classification_notes: A monolinear sans balanced between grotesque and geometric construction, positioned by the foundry as a reaffirmation of French style within European lettering heritage. Sold across five widths, standard, Extended, Wide, Narrow and Condensed, 80 fonts in total.
summary: A monolinear sans balanced between grotesque and geometric, built as an 80-font system across five widths.
description: Aiglon sets out to reaffirm French typographic style within a wider European lettering tradition, an open, sober sans that stays recognisable rather than neutral. Five widths, standard through to Condensed, give it 80 fonts in total, plus numerals in squares and a set of arrows and geometric dingbats for signage-style work.
foundry_blurb: Typofonderie call Aiglon a profoundly European French typeface, directly influenced by lettering tradition and built to reaffirm French style within European heritage.

name: Allumi
classification_notes: A wide-bodied display sans with machined, laser-cut curves, extended by Allumi Extended and by the multicolour Allumi Inline and Allumi Extended Inline released in 2021.
summary: A wide-bodied display sans with machined, laser-cut curves, extended into inline and multicolour cuts.
description: Allumi runs from a set of hairline weights up to Black, its curves cut with an industrial, machined precision. Allumi Extended widens the same design, and the 2021 Inline additions turn it into a multicolour display family for layered headline treatments.
foundry_blurb: Typofonderie describe Allumi Extended as a wide-bodied sans with machined curves and laser cuts, with Allumi Inline released in 2021 as a multicolour display family.

name: Caslonian
classification_notes: Not a purist Caslon revival but an exaggerated homage, begun in 2015 for an Estée Lauder brand project and developed with reference to the Fonderie Caslon in Paris and ITC's 1970s and 80s Caslon reworkings. Sold in four optical sizes, XL, L, M and S, each with an Open stylistic companion that colours the counters of overlapping strokes.
summary: An exaggerated homage to Caslon, more Caslon than a purist revival, offered in four optical sizes with an Open colouring option.
description: Caslonian pushes the details that make a Caslon a Caslon rather than staying faithful to any single historical cut, closer in spirit to ITC's 1970s and 80s Caslon reworkings. XL, L, M and S optical sizes cover poster to text use, and the Open companion lets the illuminated counters of overlapping strokes print in a second colour.
foundry_blurb: Typofonderie describe Caslonian as a tribute to Caslon and to ITC's historical reworkings, with Caslonian Open allowing the illuminated open parts of letters to print in different colours where strokes overlap.

name: Audace
subcategory: geometric display sans, organic and nature-inspired
classification_notes: A display sans positioned by the foundry between geometry and shapes inspired by nature, in five styles.
summary: A display sans that sits between geometric construction and shapes borrowed from nature.
description: Audace is built for headline presence rather than text, with a design brief the foundry describes as living between geometry and natural form. Regular through Extra Bold, with italic, cover its range.
foundry_blurb: Typofonderie present Audace as living between geometry and shapes inspired by nature, a design that corresponds to today's taste.
